idiom_name: enum Edit { ... } with a match-based interpreter and a Vec<Edit> history
implementation_notes: The Rust-idiomatic replacement for a command hierarchy: the request set is an enum whose variants carry the parameters, and execution is a match over it, so the compiler proves every variant is handled and the log is a Vec that needs no allocation per command and can derive Clone or serde for replay. The Book presents enums as values that are exactly one of a fixed set of possibilities with per-variant data, which is precisely a closed command set; the trait-object form is only needed when commands must be contributed from outside the crate.
pitfalls: The enum closes the command set: a new request is a compile-time event for every match, which is the intended exhaustiveness trade - do not add a catch-all arm.
Variants store owned parameters, so a replayed edit may reference positions that no longer exist; validate on apply rather than assuming the captured state is current.
A history of edits is not a snapshot: undo needs the exact previous values (for example the deleted text) captured when execute ran.

variants.name: Box<dyn Command> trait objects (classic form)
variants.idiom_name: trait Command with execute/undo and a Vec<Box<dyn Command>> invoker
variants.implementation_notes: The GoF structure translated to Rust: a Command trait with execute and undo, one struct per request, and an invoker holding Vec<Box<dyn Command>> - the same dynamic-dispatch shape the Book uses for a Vec<Box<dyn Draw>> of heterogeneous components. Choose it when commands arrive from outside the crate (plugins, scripting), own heterogeneous state, or must be registered dynamically; the cost is a vtable indirection, a heap allocation per command and object-safety constraints.
pitfalls: A trait stops being object-safe as soon as a method is generic or returns Self; keep the command trait narrow and push variation into the implementing structs.
The command borrows its receiver mutably for its lifetime, so two commands over the same document cannot run concurrently without an internal Mutex or a single owning thread.
Box<dyn Command> erases the concrete type (no downcast without Any), so descriptions, ids and serialisation must be added explicitly to the trait.
